result.title: Physically Admissible Generative Flow Matching for Sparse Flow Reconstruction
result.summary: Reconstructing full fluid velocity fields from sparse, localized observations is a severely ill-posed inverse problem: most of the spatial domain remains unobserved, discrete conservation laws must hold strictly, and predictive uncertainty must be reliable. Existing generative models typically enforce physical constraints only at the terminal output or via soft penalties, leaving intermediate generative trajectories unconstrained. We introduce Feasible Subspace Consistency (FSC), a framework that preserves physical admissibility as an invariant of continuous generative dynamics: tangent-space matching confines the entire ODE trajectory to the discrete conservation manifold, while mass-orthonormal coordinates preserve the kinetic-energy metric. Sparse reconstruction then reduces to amortized posterior transport in the latent space of a frozen FSC prior, ensuring every posterior sample inherits incompressibility and boundary conditions without per-sample projection loops. We validate FSC on a periodic Kolmogorov flow, where exact spectral projection isolates path tangency and metric isometry, and a wall-bounded cylinder wake with immersed obstacles, realized via matrix-free iterative projection. FSC prevents the mode-coverage collapse induced by terminal projection (increasing mode coverage from $0.000$ to $0.790$) while eliminating high-wavenumber spectral distortion. In sparse reconstruction, amortized FSC reduces global relative error by $50\%$ and $46\%$, and sensor residuals by $63\%$ and $55\%$, relative to the unconditioned prior, while delivering calibrated, spatially heterogeneous uncertainty.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Feasible Subspace Consistency 框架，用切空间匹配把 flow matching 的整条 ODE 轨迹约束在离散守恒流形上，并在冻结先验的 latent 空间中做摊销后验输运，用于稀疏流场重建。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉推理无直接关联，但其「让 latent 生成轨迹全程满足结构不变量、而非仅在输出端校正」的思路，可能为 LVR 中如何保持中间推理状态的任务必要信息提供形式化参照，可供核查。
